stories.name: Fatima M.
stories.title: Early Detection Saved Her Life
stories.challenge: Fatima had no symptoms and no reason to suspect she had Hepatitis B. Like many Tanzanians, she was unaware of her status and had never been tested. She had heard of hepatitis but thought it only affected 'other people.' When she got sick with what seemed like flu, doctors couldn't diagnose her condition.
stories.howTHAHelped: Through a KAPIME community screening session in her neighborhood, Fatima learned about hepatitis and decided to get tested. The screening revealed she was Hepatitis B positive. THA connected her with healthcare providers who started her on treatment immediately. She also received counseling on managing her condition and protecting her family.
stories.whereNow: Fatima is on consistent treatment and her viral load is undetectable. She has become a community advocate, encouraging others in her neighborhood to get tested. She regularly attends KAPIME screening sessions and shares her story to reduce stigma.
stories.quote: I could have died without knowing my status. KAPIME gave me my life back. Now I'm helping others get tested too.
stories.impact: Fatima has personally brought 15 community members for testing, and 3 have been diagnosed with Hepatitis B and started treatment.

stories.name: Hassan K.
stories.title: Finding Hope in Peer Support
stories.challenge: Hassan was a recent college graduate struggling with severe anxiety and depression. He felt isolated, disconnected, and didn't know who to talk to. The mental health stigma in his community made him afraid to seek help. He worried people would think he was 'weak' or 'crazy.' He contemplated ending his life.
stories.howTHAHelped: A friend invited Hassan to a Life Unlocked youth club meeting. For the first time, he found people his age facing similar challenges, without judgment. He learned coping strategies, attended counseling sessions with THA's trained psychologists, and built a support network. Over time, his anxiety diminished and he found meaning through helping other young people in the club.
stories.whereNow: Hassan is now a peer supporter with Life Unlocked, leading weekly support meetings for university students. He's pursuing his passion in psychology and plans to formalize his training. He volunteers 12 hours per week with THA.
stories.quote: Life Unlocked gave me tools to manage my anxiety and a community that understands. Now I'm helping others find the same hope.
stories.impact: Hassan has supported 45+ young people, with many reporting significant improvements in their mental health and life direction.

stories.name: Amina S.
stories.title: Breaking Silence, Building Strength
stories.challenge: Amina had experienced trauma and depression for years but never spoke about it. In her community, mental health wasn't discussed, and suffering in silence was the norm. She felt trapped, ashamed, and believed no one would understand. She spent most days alone and contemplated ending her pain permanently.
stories.howTHAHelped: Through a Talk To Heal community dialogue circle, Amina heard other women sharing their stories. For the first time, she realized she wasn't alone. She connected with a trained peer supporter and later received counseling. The dialogue circles became her lifeline, a space where she could speak freely without judgment.
stories.whereNow: Amina is now an advocate for mental health in her community. She co-facilitates Talk To Heal dialogue circles and has trained as a peer supporter. She speaks openly about her mental health journey, inspiring others to seek help. She's working on starting a women's mental health support group.
stories.quote: Talk To Heal saved me when I had no hope left. Now I'm helping others find their voice too.
stories.impact: Amina has directly helped 30+ people access mental health support and has become a leading voice against mental health stigma in her community.

stories.name: David M.
stories.title: Vaccination Prevented His Family's Suffering
stories.challenge: David lost his sister to liver complications from untreated Hepatitis B when he was 16. He watched his family suffer through her illness and death. Years later, David didn't know his own Hepatitis B status and was terrified of facing the same fate or unknowingly transmitting the virus to his own children.
stories.howTHAHelped: Through KAPIME, David got tested and learned he was Hepatitis B positive, but with early intervention possible. He started treatment and was vaccinated. THA health ambassadors helped him educate his extended family about the importance of testing and vaccination. His children were vaccinated, ensuring they wouldn't face what he did.
stories.whereNow: David is in remission with undetectable viral load. More importantly, his entire extended family, all 32 people, has been tested through KAPIME sessions. Three additional cases were discovered early and are now receiving treatment. His family is now hepatitis B negative and protected through vaccination.
stories.quote: I couldn't save my sister, but KAPIME is helping me save my family and my community.
stories.impact: David's advocacy has led to 89 people in his extended network getting tested, with 5 cases diagnosed early and 34 people vaccinated and protected.
